mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks (-41.3 to -37.6). This autoregressive momentum reflects an ongoing recovery in discretionary trips that should persist mechanically into the next four weeks absent a new shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the last 28 days despite three prior weeks of improvement.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses above -30 (i.e., recovers past the -30 threshold as seen at t-0w), this signals relaxed transit restrictions or reduced fear of crowding, which directly enables more retail and recreation trips over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -30 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -29.6 at t-0w, crossing -30 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks following a TRANSIT crossing above -30, or declines despite the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous week-on-week increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicate restored commuting patterns that jointly generate incidental retail footfall (lunch, after-work errands) exceeding the effect of either series alone, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved for three straight weeks while WORKPLACES recovered from t-1w dip at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days even when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise concurrently for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has declined each of the last three weeks (12.4 to 10.6), indicating reduced home-confinement behavior and lower risk aversion. In a gradual reopening regime, this behavioral shift is expected to spill over into higher retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 12.4 to 10.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days despite continued RESIDENTIAL decline, or the mechanism holds only during tightening regimes.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility, despite partial recovery, remains deeply suppressed (-59.1 at t-0w) and worsened mid-period, consistent with autumn weather reducing outdoor substitution for recreation. This should push some recreation demand indoors, modestly supporting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as outdoor options wane.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -55 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stayed below -58 for all four weeks in snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next two weeks while PARKS stays persistently depressed below -55.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has improved steadily and sharply (-17.7 to -9.9), suggesting relaxation of essential-only movement policies. If this pace of improvement (greater than 2 points per week) continues, it signals broader policy loosening that will extend to retail and recreation venues within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 2 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose roughly 3 points per week over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week of GROCERY_PHARM sustaining a greater-than-2-point weekly improvement.

mechanism_narrative: The rate of RETAIL_REC improvement decelerated between t-2w and t-1w (only +0.4) before accelerating again at t-0w (+4.1), suggesting a saturation effect where behavioral adaptation to reopening slows unless reinforced by workplace mobility; if WORKPLACES drops again, RETAIL_REC momentum will stall within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -33.0 to -36.9 at t-1w before recovering
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next week even after a WORKPLACES drop exceeding 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in TRANSIT and declining RESIDENTIAL together indicate increased out-of-home mobility capacity and reduced confinement simultaneously, a combination that historically compounds to drive stronger RETAIL_REC gains than either series predicts alone, over a four-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose each week while RESIDENTIAL fell each week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days despite concurrent TRANSIT rises and RESIDENTIAL declines across all four weeks.
